- When sentiment is consistently bullish (1.00) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–2% of recent mean or median.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often over-estimates continuation; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average of last 5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (0.00) mid-period, model frequently fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Model over-anticipates mean reversion in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) — use 3-day exponential smoothing to dampen short-term volatility.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 7 days as baseline for correction.
- Avoid forecasting beyond 10-day horizon without sentiment confirmation — if sentiment is weak, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent 14-day moving average.
